newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China diesel import tariffs back to 6.0-pct in Q2.
newsitem.headline: China diesel import tariffs back to 6.0-pct in Q2.

text.p: China will end a temporary 3.0-percent tariff rate on diesel imports and lift the rate back to the previous 6.0 percent starting from April 1, a customs official said on Friday.

"We've set the period for the temporary rate between November last year and March this year. We are now just bringing back the original rate," said the official with the Customs Office under China's State Council.
The official in Beijing said the temporary rate was imposed last November to ease the burden on imports of high international prices amid increased domestic winter demand.
Traders did not expect the rate rise to affect imports.
"The rate will be the same as its previous level. Imports should not change because of the rate," said one Chinese trader.
As reported, tariffs for fuel oil imports will be doubled on April 1 to 6.0 percent from the current 3.0 percent.
Fuel oil import tariffs stood at 12 percent in 1996 until November when they were reduced to 3.0 percent for five months because of high international prices and strong domestic demand.
